SMC pathways
The Skilled Migrant Category (SMC) Resident Visa offers 3 pathways to residence. Each is designed to recognise different types of skills, experience, and contributions to New Zealand's workforce.
Points-based pathway
You must have 6 points to be eligible for the Points-based pathway. You can claim up to 6 points from either your:
qualification
income (pay), or
occupational registration (for example, if you are a chartered accountant or registered plumber).

If you cannot claim all 6 points from one of these categories, you may be able to claim an additional 1 to 3 points from skilled work experience in New Zealand. These work experience points can be combined with the points you claim from your qualification, income, or occupational registration to reach 6 points.
Skilled Work Experience pathway
This pathway is for people who have developed their skills through work experience rather than through a formal qualification (such as a university degree, diploma, or trade certificate).
To be eligible, you must have at least 5 years of directly relevant work experience, including at least 2 years of skilled work experience in New Zealand.
Trades and Technician pathway
This pathway is for people working in eligible trades or technician roles who have developed their skills through a combination of qualifications and work experience.
To be eligible, you must have a relevant qualification, and at least 4 years of post-qualification work experience, including at least 18 months of skilled work experience in New Zealand.
Points-based pathway
Skilled resident points
Skilled resident points are the points you need to be eligible to apply for a Points-based SMC Resident Visa.
You need 6 skilled resident points from your skills and work in New Zealand.
If you are invited to apply, you must provide evidence that you qualify for the points you are claiming.
You can claim:
3 to 6 points from 1 skill category — either your qualification, New Zealand occupational registration, or income, and
up to 3 more points from skilled work experience in New Zealand (if required).
Qualification
You can use your qualification to claim points if it:
is a New Zealand qualification recognised on the New Zealand Qualifications and Credentials Framework (NZQCF)
has had an International Qualification Assessment (IQA) from the New Zealand Qualifications Authority (NZQA) , or
is on the List of Qualifications Exempt from Assessment (LQEA).
Check if you need an International Qualification Assessment
You can claim between 4 to 6 points depending on the highest level of qualification you have, and if it was gained in New Zealand or internationally.

Income

You can use the income (or pay) from your current New Zealand job or job offer to claim points, if the income from the job is at least 1.5 times the SMC wage threshold. You can claim between 3 and 6 points from your income.

If you earn enough to claim 6 points from your income the current SMC wage threshold will apply. If you need to claim additional points from skilled work experience, the SMC wage threshold that applies to you can be lower, depending on when you started gaining this work experience and if it was within the eligible timeframe.

Claiming points for skilled work experience in New Zealand

If you cannot claim 6 points from your income, you can use your skilled work experience in New Zealand to reach 6 points — you cannot use your occupational registration or qualifications to claim more points.
Example
Elle is claiming 4 points for being paid 2 times the SMC wage threshold. She needs to claim 2 more points from skilled work experience to get to 6 points.

To claim 2 points from skilled work experience, she must have 1.5 years of work experience in New Zealand paid at 2 times the SMC wage threshold. The SMC wage threshold that applies to her will depend on when she started her skilled work experience.

Elle started working in New Zealand in October 2023, which means she must earn at least NZD $59.32 an hour (2 times the SMC wage threshold at that time) to begin counting her skilled work experience – and to claim 4 points from her income.

Skilled work experience requirements
Your skilled work experience must:
be in a full-time job (at least 30 hours a week)
meet the minimum pay requirement for your job's ANZSCO skill level (or income multiple if you are claiming points for income), and
closely match the job title and description for your occupation in ANZSCO.

Note
If you took an extended period of leave during your skilled work experience period, you may still be able to include this time if it was for parental leave, ACC leave or sick leave.
What does not count as work experience
You cannot include any work experience you gained while on an India Iconic Work Visa or India Skilled Work Visa.
Minimum pay requirement
If you are claiming points for your qualification or occupational registration, the minimum pay you need depends on your job's ANZSCO skill level:
ANZSCO skill levels 1 to 3 jobs must have been paid at least the SMC wage threshold
ANZSCO skill levels 4 to 5 jobs must have been paid at least 1.5 times the SMC wage threshold.

The SMC wage threshold that applies to you will depend on when you started gaining skilled work experience and if it was within the eligible timeframe. You can find out more about the SMC wage threshold and which rate applies to you here:

Skilled Work Experience pathway
The Skilled Work Experience pathway allows you to get New Zealand residence from your work experience, without needing a formal qualification like a PhD or Master's degree.
You are eligible for the Skilled Work Experience pathway if you:
work in or have a job offer for an ANZSCO skill level 1 to 3 occupation paid at least 1.1 times the SMC wage threshold
have at least 3 years of relevant work experience in an ANZSCO skill level 1 to 3 occupation, and
have an additional 2 years of skilled work experience in New Zealand in an ANZSCO skill level 1 to 3 occupation paid at least 1.1 times the SMC wage threshold.
Find your job's skill level

The SMC wage threshold that applies to you will depend on when you started gaining skilled work experience and if it was within the eligible timeframe. You can find out more about the SMC wage threshold and which rate applies to you here:
The SMC wage threshold
What relevant and skilled work experience means
Relevant work experience is work experience related to your current job or job offer. You can not include self-employment as relevant work experience.
Skilled work experience is work experience related to your current job or job offer, completed in New Zealand and paid at the required amount.
What does not count as work experience
You cannot include any work experience you gained while on an India Iconic Work Visa or India Skilled Work Visa.
Amber and Red List jobs
If your current job or job offer is on the Amber List, there are additional requirements you must meet to be eligible for this pathway.
If your current job or job offer is on the Red List, or is an ANZSCO skill level 4 or 5 occupation, you are not eligible for this pathway.
Find out what jobs are on the Amber and Red List, and what additional requirements apply here:
Red and Amber List occupations
Timeframe for gaining work experience
You must have gained your work experience within a set timeframe.

For relevant work experience this timeframe is 10 years, counted back from the date you apply for residence. For example, if you need 3 years of relevant work experience, this experience must have been gained within the 10 years immediately before you apply for residence.

For skilled work experience this timeframe is twice as long as the amount of experience you need, counted back from the date you apply for residence. For example, if you need 2 years of skilled work experience, this experience must have been gained within the 4 years immediately before you apply for residence.
Note
If you took an extended period of leave during your skilled work experience period, you may still be able to include this time if it was for parental leave, ACC leave or sick leave.

Trades and Technician pathway
The Trades and Technician pathway allows you to get New Zealand residence if you work in a trades and technicians job.
You are eligible for the Trades and Technician pathway if you:
work in an eligible trades and technician occupation paid at least the SMC wage threshold
have a relevant qualification that is level 4, comparable to level 4, or higher than level 4 on the NZQCF
have at least 2.5 years of relevant, post-qualification work experience in an ANZSCO skill level 1 to 3 occupation, and
have an additional 1.5 years of post-qualification, skilled work experience in New Zealand paid at least the SMC wage threshold.
Eligible occupations for the SMC Trades and Technician pathway

The SMC wage threshold that applies to you will depend on when you started gaining skilled work experience and if it was within the eligible timeframe. You can find out more about the SMC wage threshold and which rate applies to you here:
The SMC wage threshold
What relevant and skilled work experience means
Relevant work experience is work experience related to your current job or job offer. You can not include self-employment as relevant work experience.
Skilled work experience is work experience related to your current job or job offer, completed in New Zealand and paid at the required amount.
What does not count as work experience
You cannot include any work experience you gained while on an India Iconic Work Visa or India Skilled Work Visa.
Requirements for New Zealand qualifications
If your Trades and Technicians qualification is from New Zealand, it must be either:
at least 120 credits on the NZQCF, or
less than 120 credits but with multiple prerequisite qualifications that together make at least 120 credits.
Alert
If you were awarded credits in recognition of prior learning, they will not count towards the 120 credit requirement.
Requirements for international qualifications

If you have a qualification from outside of New Zealand, there are no credit requirements but you must have an International Qualification Assessment (IQA) from the New Zealand Qualifications Authority (NZQA).

Timeframe for gaining work experience
You must have gained your work experience within a set timeframe.

For relevant work experience this timeframe is 10 years, counted back from the date you apply for residence. For example, if you need 3 years of relevant work experience, this experience must have been gained within the 10 years immediately before you apply for residence.

For skilled work experience this timeframe is twice as long as the amount of experience you need, counted back from the date you apply for residence. For example, if you need 2 years of skilled work experience, this experience must have been gained within the 4 years immediately before you apply for residence.
Note
If you took an extended period of leave during your skilled work experience period, you may still be able to include this time if it was for parental leave, ACC leave or sick leave.
Requirements for all pathways
All SMC pathways require you to:
be aged 55 or younger
have an offer of, or be working in, a full-time skilled job with an accredited employer
be in good health
be of good character
have a genuine relationship with your partner and dependent children, if including them, and
speak and understand English.
Age
You must be aged 55 or younger when you apply.
We check your identity document to confirm your age.
Current job or job offer
You must be working in a skilled job, or have a job offer for one.
To be considered a skilled job, it must:
be with an accredited employer
be full-time and (for at least 30 hours a week)
permanent or fixed-term for at least 12 months, or a contract or continuous contracts for at least 6 months, and
meet any pay requirements for your SMC pathway.
Accredited employer list
What is ANZSCO

The Australian and New Zealand Standard Classification of Occupations (ANZSCO) list grades jobs according to skill level. ANZSCO skill levels range from 1 to 5, with 1 being the most skilled and 5 being less skilled.
The job title and description for your job should mostly match the job title and description in ANZSCO.
Find your job's skill level
Beware of scams
Job offer scams are common in India and South Asia. Make sure your job offer is genuine.
Protecting yourself from immigration scams
Health
You, and anyone else included in your application, must be in good health.
Why you may need to provide evidence you are in good health
You, and anyone else included aged 11 or older, must complete a chest X-ray and medical examination.
Dependent children included in your application and aged:
10 or younger, must get a medical examination, but do not need a chest X-ray unless we or your panel physician ask for one
11 to 14, must get a medical examination and a chest X-ray, but only need a blood test if we or your panel physician ask for one.
How to get an X-ray or medical examination
If you have provided medical certificates to us before and those certificates were issued within the last 3 years, you may not need to provide them again.
Evidence of a chest X-ray or medical examination must be less than 3 months old when we receive it (if not used for a previous visa application).
Character
You, and anyone else included in your application, must be of good character.
If you, and anyone else included, are aged 17 or older, you must provide police certificates that are less than 6 months old when you apply.
If you have a criminal conviction, or are a security risk to New Zealand, we might not give you a visa.
Character requirements for New Zealand visas
You must get police certificates from:
countries you are a citizen of, and
countries where you have spent 12 months or more in over the last 10 years — even if those 12 months were not all in one stay.
Police certificates must show any criminal records you have had at any time in any of these countries — not only in the last 10 years.
If we ask for a new police certificate when processing your application, you will need to send us a new one.
Police certificates
Note
Your police certificates must be less than 6 months old when you submit your application. Allow yourself enough time to get these certificates.
Partner and dependent children
If you include your partner and dependent children aged 24 or younger in your application, you must have a genuine relationship with them.
You must be able to prove your relationship to your partner and dependent children aged 24 or younger.
If you are separated from your dependent children's other parent, or the other parent is not applying for residence with you, you also must show that you have permission to bring them to New Zealand.
Find out more about how to do this here:
Partnership and how to prove it
Bringing children

If you are including your partner in your application you need to have lived with them for at least 12 months. If you have not lived with them for 12 months, we may approve your application but delay your partner's application to allow them time to meet this requirement.
If your partner or dependent children already have, or are applying for, a work, student or visitor visa based on their relationship to you, you must include them in your residence application.

If your children are already in New Zealand, they must be here lawfully, even if you do not include them in your application. If they are not, for example they do not have a valid visa, your application will be declined.
If your child stays in New Zealand after their visa expires
English language
You must be able to speak and understand English.
You can meet this requirement through:
your citizenship
where you studied and the qualifications you gained, or
English language tests.
The results of your English language test must:
meet the minimum score we set
be no more than 2 years old when you apply.
Find out about the requirements around citizenship, study and qualifications, the test results required, and how to buy English language lessons:
English language requirements for skilled residence visas
English language requirements for family
Your partner and dependent children aged 16 or older must also be able to speak and understand English.
When we assess your application, we may ask for more proof of your and your family's ability to speak English. If we do, you and your family may have to sit tests and send us the results.

If you are including family members and they do not meet the English requirements, you will need to buy English language lessons for them to learn in New Zealand. You can choose to buy lessons in your visa application form. We will let you know how to pay for the lessons after you apply.
Note

If you or someone included in your application has an occupational registration that is eligible for points under the Points-based pathway, your English language test results can be up to 5 years old (for the person who has the registration). You can do this even if you are applying under another pathway.

Income
If you are claiming points for income you can provide:

contract or contracts (without breaks) adding up to 6 months or more

Skilled work experience in New Zealand

Provide an employment agreement and job description for each period of skilled work experience in New Zealand, including your key tasks and responsibilities. These documents must show your name, occupation, the name of the employer, hours and pay rate for each job.

Provide an Inland Revenue Department (IRD) summary of earnings or IRD tax statement covering all your periods of skilled work experience in New Zealand. Your IRD summary of earnings must be up to the date you apply and should provide monthly breakdowns.
Tip

Skilled work experience in New Zealand must be gained within the eligible timeframe. This is usually twice as long as the amount of experience you need, counted back from the date you apply for residence.
Relevant work experience
Provide an employment agreement and job description showing the occupation, hours and rate of pay for each work period.
Provide a summary of earnings or tax statement from the respective government authority for each work experience claimed confirming the period of work and income over any period of work.

If you cannot provide tax records for your overseas work experience, you can provide a certificate of service from your employer instead. Certificates of service cannot be used as evidence of New Zealand work experience.
Tip
Relevant work experience must be from the past 10 years, counted back from the date you apply for residence.

How to apply
Follow these steps to complete your application online.
Before you start, make sure you have all the required documents. This will help avoid delays.
Step 1: Submit your expression of interest
Before you submit an Expression of Interest (EOI), make sure you meet the requirements for at least 1 of the SMC pathways.
If you need an International Qualification Assessment (IQA), apply for one before submitting your EOI. You will need to include the IQA reference number in your EOI.
Check if you need an International Qualification Assessment
Submit an Expression of Interest
There is no fee to submit an EOI.
You do not need to complete your EOI all at once. You can save it and come back later.
Step 2: Receive an invitation to apply
After you submit your EOI, we will tell you immediately whether you meet the requirements.
If you meet the requirements, you can continue to the residence application. We will also email you an invitation to apply (ITA) with further information.
You must submit your visa application within 4 months of receiving your ITA. You must apply under the SMC pathway that you have been invited for.
Note
If you do not apply within 4 months, you will need to submit a new EOI.
Step 3: Gather your supporting documents
The section 'Who can apply' explains the requirements for this visa. The 'Documents you need' section explains what evidence you will need to provide.
Step 4: Submit your application and pay the fee
To apply online, click on the link in your invitation to apply (ITA).
You will need to log into your account, if you are not already logged in.
You can then fill in your application, upload your documents and pay the applicable fees.
Check the 'Cost and processing time' section for fees.
Step 5: Wait for our decision
We will let you know if we need more information to process your application.
Waiting for a visa
Check the 'Cost and processing time' section for wait times.
Note
If you are already in New Zealand, you must have a valid visa.
If you have not applied for a new temporary visa, we may give you a Skilled Migrant Category Interim Visa.
Skilled Migrant Category Interim Visa Information
Step 6: Receive our decision
We will email you when we make a decision.
If we approve your application, we will give you an eVisa and send you a copy.

You must come to New Zealand within 12 months of the date your visa is issued, if you applied for your visa outside of New Zealand.
When you arrive
Entry permission
You must apply for permission to enter New Zealand. You do this by completing a New Zealand Traveller Declaration (NZTD) form.
You can start your digital declaration any time, but the earliest you can submit it is 24 hours before starting your travel to New Zealand.
A paper declaration form is available for travellers who cannot complete it online.
New Zealand Traveller Declaration
New Zealand Customs and Biosecurity also check that you meet their entry requirements.
Arriving in New Zealand
Warning
You can be refused entry permission if you:
do not meet our character requirements
have had a change in circumstances since we issued your visa, or
refuse to let us take your photo, fingerprints or an iris scan.
What might stop you from being allowed to enter New Zealand
While you are in New Zealand
Your resident visa allows you to live, work and study in New Zealand indefinitely.
Any visa conditions that apply to you will be recorded in your eVisa. You must comply with your visa conditions.
Travel
You can travel in and out of New Zealand as many times as you like until your travel conditions expire.
Your travel conditions expire 2 years from:
the date you first arrive in New Zealand as a resident, or
the date your visa is given, if you are already in New Zealand.
To travel after that, you need to:
get a Permanent Resident Visa, or
extend your travel conditions, which would let you return to New Zealand at a later date.
Permanent Resident Visa
Check or change your resident visa conditions
Warning
If you are outside of New Zealand when your travel conditions expire, your visa will expire as well.
If your passport expires, you must apply to transfer your visa to a new passport before you can travel.
Transferring a visa to a new passport
Work
You can work in any job for any employer in New Zealand.
Study
You can study anywhere in New Zealand for any length of time.
Section 49 conditions
Section 49 conditions are extra conditions we may give to some visas, under section 49(1) of the Immigration Act 2009.
If your Skilled Migrant Category Resident Visa has section 49 conditions, they will be listed in your eVisa.
Check or change your resident visa conditions
Warning
You must not be unemployed for more than 3 months. If you lose your job, you must get another skilled job that is for at least 3 months to meet your section 49 conditions.
If you do not, we may cancel your visa and you must leave the country.
How long you can stay
A Skilled Migrant Category Resident Visa lets you stay in New Zealand indefinitely.
Staying longer
Getting a Permanent Resident Visa
After you have had a Skilled Migrant Category Resident Visa for 2 years in a row, you can apply for a Permanent Resident Visa.
Becoming a permanent resident of New Zealand
Permanent Resident Visa
Removing Section 49 conditions
If you have Section 49 conditions and want to apply for a Permanent Resident Visa, you must:
meet your section 49 conditions, then
apply to have them removed.
Request to remove section 49 conditions
To remove section 49 conditions, you — the main applicant or 'principal applicant' — will need to provide the following:
a cover letter asking Immigration New Zealand to remove your section 49 conditions and including all your current contact details
copies of valid passports for you and everyone included on your Skilled Migrant Category Resident Visa application
a letter from your employer, printed on company letterhead paper that: confirms your position and that you have been in full-time employment for the period required by your section 49 conditions
shows the contact details of the company
is dated and signed by a person authorised to confirm the status of your employment
copies of 2 recent payslips and a recent bank statement confirming your employment, or a summary of earnings from the Inland Revenue (IR).
There is no cost for removing section 49 conditions.
If we need more information, we will contact you.
You can post your request or send it by courier.

The SMC wage threshold
Find the pay rates you need to earn for the Skilled Migrant Category (SMC) Resident Visa.
What is a wage threshold?
A wage threshold is the minimum hourly pay rate you need to earn, to meet the requirements of a visa.
There are different wage thresholds for different visas. Wage thresholds for the Skilled Migrant Category Resident Visa are based on the median wage and are updated each year.
Find your hourly pay rate
You will need to know your hourly pay rate to check if you meet the SMC wage threshold. If you do not know your hourly pay rate, use the hourly pay rate calculator.
Hourly pay rate calculator
Tip
If you are paid a salary, make sure you use the maximum contracted hours stated in your employment agreement.
What SMC wage threshold do you need to meet?
You must be paid at least the SMC wage threshold:
in your current job or job offer, and
during your skilled work experience in New Zealand (if your pathway requires this).
The SMC wage threshold that applies to you depends on the pathway you are applying under. For some pathways, it also depends on when you started gaining skilled work experience in New Zealand.
You can find out more about SMC pathways here:
Getting residence through the Skilled Migrant Category
You can jump to wage threshold amounts for each SMC pathway here:
SMC wage threshold rates
You can also use our SMC wage threshold tool to find out what SMC wage threshold applies to you:
SMC wage threshold tool
If your pathway does not require skilled work experience in New Zealand

If you are claiming 6 points under the Points-based pathway and you do not need skilled work experience in New Zealand, your current job or job offer must meet the SMC wage threshold that is in place when you are invited to apply for residence.
This is usually the same date that you submit your expression of interest (EOI).
This may apply if you are claiming 6 points for:
a doctoral degree
a New Zealand master's degree
an occupational registration, or
your income.
If your pathway requires skilled work experience in New Zealand

If you are applying under an SMC pathway that requires you to have skilled work experience in New Zealand, you must meet the SMC wage threshold that was in place when you started gaining this work experience.
If your pay did not meet the SMC wage threshold when you started working in New Zealand, you can begin gaining skilled work experience later (for example if you receive a pay rise or change jobs).

Your skilled work experience starts counting when your pay meets the SMC wage threshold in place at that time. You cannot use an earlier SMC wage threshold (that was in place when you started work in New Zealand) and start meeting it later.
Key rule
Once your threshold is set, it does not change. Any further skilled work experience you complete, and the current job or job offer you use to apply, must meet or be higher than this threshold.

These tables show SMC wage threshold rates by pathway. All pay rates are hourly and in New Zealand dollars (NZD).

Timeframe for setting your SMC wage threshold
There is a limit on how far back you can go when setting your SMC wage threshold.

The skilled work experience used to set your threshold must be within the eligible timeframe for your pathway. This timeframe is twice the amount of skilled work experience you need, counted back from the date you submit your EOI.

For example, if you need 2 years of skilled work experience and you submit your EOI on 1 September 2026, the earliest you can set your threshold is 1 September 2022 (4 years before you submit your EOI).
Timeframe for counting skilled work experience
The timeframe used to set your wage threshold is different from the timeframe used to count your skilled work experience.

When setting your wage threshold, the eligible timeframe is counted back from the date you submit your EOI. However, the eligible timeframe for counting skilled work experience is counted back from the date you apply for residence.
This means you can continue gaining skilled work experience after submitting your EOI and before applying for residence.

If you change jobs
For most people, you will not need to meet a higher SMC wage threshold if you change jobs during your skilled work experience.
You must continue to meet the threshold that was set when your skilled work experience first became eligible to count.
This includes if:
you change employers, or
you get a new position with the same employer.
If your pay drops below the threshold that applies to you, that work experience cannot count towards your SMC application.
Note
You may need to meet a higher SMC wage threshold if you are applying under the Points-based pathway and change jobs from an ANZSCO skill level 1 to 3 job to a skill level 4 or 5 job.
Grace period

In some cases, the SMC wage threshold may have increased between the date you received your work visa and the date you started gaining your skilled work experience. In these instances, there is a grace period that may allow you to meet the lower threshold that was in place when you received your work visa.
When it applies
The grace period applies if:
you started gaining your skilled work experience within 5 months of your work visa being granted
the SMC wage threshold increased between the date your work visa was granted and the date you started your skilled work experience
your skilled work experience was within the eligible timeframe, and
when you started your skilled work experience, you were paid at least the SMC wage threshold that was in place when your work visa was granted.
The grace period does not apply to a variation of conditions or an AEWV Job Change.
If your pathway depends on a qualification or registration

If you are applying through the Trades and Technician pathway, or you are claiming points for occupational registration under the Points-based pathway, only skilled work experience gained after you became qualified or registered can be counted.
This is because the qualification or registration is the point when you are recognised as skilled in that job.
Work experience gained before completing the relevant qualification or gaining the required occupational registration cannot be used towards the skilled work experience requirement.
Other examples
The following examples explain how SMC wage threshold works in more complex situations.

Getting New Zealand residence through the Skilled Migrant Category (SMC)
Find out how the Skilled Migrant Category works, what the 3 pathways are, and if it is a good residence option for you.
What the Skilled Migrant Category is
The Skilled Migrant Category (SMC) is a residence visa for people who have skills New Zealand needs.
You may be able to apply for an SMC Resident Visa if you have a skilled job or job offer in New Zealand and meet the requirements for 1 of the SMC pathways.
The SMC Resident Visa lets you:
live, work and study in New Zealand indefinitely
include your partner and dependent children aged 24 or younger in your application, and
apply for a Permanent Resident Visa later, if you meet the requirements.
Is the Skilled Migrant Category right for you?
The SMC may be an option if you have a skilled job or job offer in New Zealand and 1 of the following applies to you:
you have a recognised qualification, like a bachelor's degree, master's degree or PhD
you have eligible occupational registration, like registration as a plumber or membership as a chartered accountant
you earn enough to claim points from your pay (income)
you have at least 5 years of work experience, or
you work in an eligible trades or technician role.
The 3 SMC pathways
There are 3 ways to qualify for the Skilled Migrant Category Resident Visa.
Table 1: Overview of the 3 SMC pathways
SMC pathway
This may suit you if
How it works
Points-based pathway
You have points from your qualification, occupational registration or pay
You need 6 skilled resident points. You may be able to combine points from your qualification, occupational registration, or pay with work experience in New Zealand
Skilled Work Experience pathway
You have several years of skilled work experience
You can qualify through work experience alone, if you have the required relevant work experience and skilled work experience in New Zealand
Trades and Technician pathway
You work in an eligible trades or technician role
You can qualify through a mix of an eligible trades or technician job, a relevant qualification, and post-qualification work experience
You only need to meet the requirements for 1 pathway.
Requirements all SMC applicants must meet
No matter which pathway you use, you must usually:
have a job or job offer in New Zealand
be paid a certain amount
be in good health
pass a character check (a police check), and
be able to speak and understand English.
If you include your partner or dependent children in your application, they may also need to meet health, character and English requirements.
Points-based pathway
The Points-based pathway is for people who can claim skilled resident points.
You need 6 points to be eligible. You can claim points from 1 of these skill categories:
qualifications
occupational registration
pay from your job or job offer.

Some people can get all 6 points from 1 category. For example, this may be possible if you have a PhD, a New Zealand master's degree that meets the requirements, an eligible occupational registration that requires significant training, or a very high income.
If you cannot get all 6 points from 1 category, you may be able to add points from skilled work experience in New Zealand.
Check your points
You can use our points calculator to find out how many points you can claim.
SMC points calculator
In general you will be able to claim points if you:
have a qualification that is at least a level 7 bachelor's degree or higher
have an occupational registration that requires at least 2 years of training or experience (for example, if you are a registered accountant, electrician, or plumber), or
are paid at least 1.5 times the SMC wage threshold.
Tip
You can find out more about the SMC wage threshold in the 'Common SMC terms' section of this page.
Examples
You may be able to claim 6 points in different ways:
if you have a bachelor's degree and some New Zealand skilled work experience
if you have eligible occupational registration and some New Zealand work experience
if you are paid at least 1.5 times the SMC wage threshold and have some New Zealand skilled work experience
if you have a New Zealand master's degree that you studied full-time for 30 weeks.

You cannot mix points from different skill categories. For example, you cannot combine qualification points with income points. You can only combine 1 skill category with skilled work experience in New Zealand.
If you are using New Zealand skilled work experience to claim points, it will need to have been paid at the SMC wage threshold, or higher if you are also claiming points from income.
Skilled Work Experience pathway
The Skilled Work Experience pathway is for people who have built their skills through work experience.
This pathway may suit you if you work in a skilled role and have several years of experience in that type of work.
To use this pathway, you must have:
a job or job offer in an ANZSCO skill level 1 to 3 occupation
pay of at least 1.1 times the SMC wage threshold
at least 3 years of relevant work experience, and
an additional 2 years of skilled work experience in New Zealand.
Some jobs have extra rules. If your job is on the Amber List, you must meet higher requirements. If your job is on the Red List, you cannot use this pathway.
Red and Amber list occupations
You cannot count self-employment as relevant work experience for this pathway.
Tip
You can find out what the SMC wage threshold, relevant work experience and skilled work experience mean in the 'Common SMC terms' section of this page.
Trades and Technician pathway
The Trades and Technician pathway is for people in eligible trades and technician occupations.
This pathway may suit you if you work in a practical or technical role and have both a relevant qualification and work experience.
Eligible roles may include some jobs in areas like:
construction
engineering
manufacturing
automotive trades
technical support roles.
Eligible occupations for the SMC Trades and Technician pathway
To use this pathway, you must have:
a job in an eligible trades or technician occupation
pay of at least the SMC wage threshold
a relevant qualification at level 4 or higher , or comparable to level 4 or higher
at least 2.5 years of relevant post-qualification work experience, and
an additional 1.5 years of post-qualification skilled work experience in New Zealand.
You cannot count self-employment as relevant work experience for this pathway.
Tip
You can find out what the SMC wage threshold, relevant work experience and skilled work experience mean in the 'Common SMC terms' section of this page.
How to know which pathway may fit you
The best SMC pathway for you will depend on what skills you have.
If you have a degree or occupational registration

The Points-based pathway may be the best place to start. Check how many points your qualification or registration is worth, then check whether you need New Zealand skilled work experience to reach 6 points.
If you are highly paid

The Points-based pathway may be the best place to start. Your income may give you enough points to apply, or it may give you some points that you can combine with skilled work experience in New Zealand.
If you have strong work experience but do not have a degree
The Skilled Work Experience pathway may be the best place to start. This pathway is designed for people who can show they have developed their skills through work experience.
If you work in a trades or technician role
The Trades and Technician pathway may be the best place to start. You need to check whether your occupation is eligible and whether your qualification and work experience meet the requirements.
If you are eligible for more than 1 pathway
If you have a combination of skills, for example if you have a master's degree and a lot of work experience, you may be eligible for more than 1 SMC pathway.
You can find guidance on what to do in this situation, as well as information about other New Zealand residence pathways here:
Getting New Zealand residence through your skills
Common SMC terms
Accredited employer
An accredited employer is an employer approved by Immigration New Zealand to hire migrants. For SMC, your skilled job or job offer must be with an accredited employer.
ANZSCO (Australian and New Zealand Standard Classification of Occupations)
ANZSCO is a system used to classify jobs by skill level. Many SMC requirements depend on whether your job is ANZSCO skill level 1 to 3, or ANZSCO skill level 4 to 5.
Find your job's skill level
SMC wage threshold

The SMC wage threshold is the pay rate used to check whether your job or work experience meets the wage requirements. Some pathways require you to be paid the SMC wage threshold. Others require a higher rate, such as 1.1, 1.2 or 1.5 times the SMC wage threshold. The SMC wage threshold that applies to you will depend on which pathway you are applying for, and when you started gaining skilled work experience in New Zealand (if applicable).
You can find which SMC wage threshold applies to you here:
The SMC wage threshold
Skilled resident points
For the SMC Points-based pathway, we use a points system called skilled resident points. You need 6 points to be eligible for an SMC Resident Visa.
Expression of interest (EOI)
An expression of interest is the first step in applying for the SMC Resident Visa. If your EOI shows you meet the requirements, you may be invited to apply for residence.
Relevant work experience
Relevant work experience is work experience related to your current job or job offer.
Skilled work experience
Skilled work experience is work experience related to your current job or job offer, completed in New Zealand, and paid at the required amount.
What to do next
Check which SMC pathway may fit you.
Check the full Skilled Migrant Category Resident Visa requirements.
Gather evidence for the pathway you want to apply under.
Submit an EOI if you meet the requirements.
You can find all details of the SMC Resident Visa requirements, including what evidence you will need to apply on the Skilled Migrant Category Resident Visa page.
